questions.question: A man sells potatoes at ₹27 per kg, which he bought at ₹25 per kg. He also uses a faulty weight and each time gives 800 g instead of 1 kg. His actual gain percentage is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price = ₹27 per kg

Cost price = ₹25 per kg

Weight discrepancy = 800 g instead of 1 kg

**Formula Used:**

Gain Percentage = [(Selling Price - Cost Price) ÷ Cost Price] × 100

**Calculation:**

Actual selling price for 1 kg = ₹27

But he gives only 800 g for 1 kg.

So, the selling price for 800 g = ₹27

Cost of 1kg = ₹25

But he is giving only 800gm to the customer, So

Cost of 800gm = 25/1000 × 800 = ₹20

⇒ Actual Gain Percentage = [(27 - 20) ÷ 20] × 100 = 35%

**So, his actual gain percentage is 35%.**

• 1/v = 1/f - 1/u
 
• Where 'v' is the image distance.

• 1/v = -1/25 + 1/50
 
• 1/v = (-2 + 1)/50

• v = -50/3 cm = -16.67 cm
 
 
 
• **Magnification formula:**
 
 
• Magnification (M) = v/u = hᵢ/h₀
 
• Where 'hᵢ' is the image size.

• M = 1/3
 
 
 
• **Image size:**
 
 
• hᵢ = M * h₀
 
• hᵢ = (1/3) * 3.0 cm
 
• hᵢ = 1.0 cm
 
 
 
• So, the size of the image formed is 1.0 cm.

⇒ 2l + 2/3l = 64

⇒ 8/3l = 64

⇒ l = 64 × 3/8

⇒ l = 24

Width: w = 1/3 × l

⇒ w = 1/3 × 24

⇒ w = 8 cm

**The width of the rectangle is 8 cm.**

questions.question: The radius of curvature of a convex mirror of focal length 2 m is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.0m**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** radius of curvature (R) of a spherical mirror is related to its focal length (f**) by the following equation:

 
 
• **R = 2f**
 
 
 
• In this case, the focal length (f) of the convex mirror is given as 2 m.
 
• Therefore, **the radius of curvature (R) is:**
 
• **R = 2 * 2 m = 4 m**
 
• So, the correct answer is 4.0 m.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Spherical Mirrors and Their Properties**

 
 
• **Concave Mirror:** A concave mirror curves inwards, like the inside of a spoon. It can focus light rays to a single point.
 
• **Convex Mirror:** A convex mirror curves outwards, like the back of a spoon. It diverges light rays, making objects appear smaller and providing a wider field of view.
 
 
 
• **Key Terms**
 
 
• **Focal Length (f):** The distance between the mirror's surface and its focal point (the point where parallel light rays converge after reflection in a concave mirror, or appear to diverge from in a convex mirror).
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R):** The radius of the sphere from which the mirror is a part. It's the distance between the mirror's surface and the center of curvature (the center of that sphere).

questions.question: A cross between a tall plant (TT) and short plant (tt) resulted in F1 progeny which were all tall plants because:

options.text: The plant height is governed by T and t
The plant height is governed by t only
The plant height is governed by T only
The plant height is governed by T or t

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The plant height is governed by T or t**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A cross between a tall plant (TT) and short plant (tt) **resulted in all tall offspring because the plant height is governed by T only**
 
• This is an **example of a monohybrid cross**
 
• In** Mendelian genetics, the allele (TT) represents tallness and the allele (tt) represents shortness. **
 
• When** two traits of a character are cr**ossed, the (F₁₎ plants only show the dominant trait.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae8821537f7860391e81403eebc4737b3f817e488db1d36a30e17c796b8cc401.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• '​Pure' plants refer to the homozygous condition in plants and 'hybrid' refers to the heterozygous plants.
 
• Homozygous - It is the condition in which the pair of alleles determining a phenotype is identical, either both dominant (TT) or both recessive (tt).
 
• Heterozygous - It is the condition where 2 different types of alleles are present, one dominant and one recessive (Tt).
 
• When a pure tall plant (TT) is crossed with a pure short plant (tt), the F1 generation produces heterozygous tall (Tt) plants.
 
• Upon selfing the F1 generation, that is, crossing two heterozygous tall plants, the following numbers of the F2 generation are obtained phenotypically:
 
 
• Three tall plants and one short plant
 
 
 
• Whereas, genotypically, the following ratio is obtained:
 
 
• One pure tall plant, two heterozygous tall plants, and one pure short plant.
 
 
 
• Therefore, considering the genotype, the ratio of pure tall plants to pure short plants in the F2 generation is 1:1

questions.question: Mr. X travelled 220 km, 250 km and 140 km at a speed of 11 km/h, 5 km/h and 7 km/h, respectively. Find his average speed in km/h.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Distances travelled: 220 km, 250 km, 140 km

Speeds: 11 km/h, 5 km/h, 7 km/h

**Formula Used**

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**Calculation**

Total distance = 220 + 250 + 140 = 610 km

Time for 220 km = 220 / 11 = 20 hours

Time for 250 km = 250 / 5 = 50 hours

Time for 140 km = 140 / 7 = 20 hours

Total time = 20 + 50 + 20 = 90 hours

⇒ Average speed = Total distance / Total time = 610 / 90 = 6(7)/(9) km/h.

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.solution:
**Given**

Original time = 15 days

Actual time taken = 20 days

**Formula Used**

Work = People × Days

**Calculation**

x × 15 = (x - 3) × 20

⇒ 15x = 20x - 60

⇒ 60 = 20x - 15x

⇒ 60 = 5x

⇒ x = 60 / 5

⇒ x = 12

**Thus, the value of X is 12.**

sqrt {2 + sqrt {2 + sqrt {2 + ldots ldots ldots .} } }

Let sqrt {2 + sqrt {2 + ldots ldots ldots .} } be y.

⇒ y = √(2 + y)

Squaring both sides

⇒ y² = 2 + y

⇒ y² – y – 2 = 0

⇒ (y – 2) (y + 1) = 0

⇒ y = 2 or y = -1
